title: Domain I: Regulatory & Compliance - CPPB Domain I: Regulatory & Compliance - UCC: Warranties
subject: CPPB Domain I: Regulatory & Compliance

questions.q: Under the Uniform Commercial Code (UCC), which type of warranty is created when a seller affirms a specific fact, makes a promise relating to the goods, or provides a sample or model of the goods?
options: Implied warranty of fitness for a particular purpose
questions.explain: An express warranty is explicitly created by the seller's affirmations, promises, descriptions, or the use of samples/models regarding the goods being sold. Implied warranties exist automatically by operation of law.
questions.subject: CPPB Domain I: Regulatory & Compliance

questions.q: A public buyer purchases a specialized heavy-duty pump after explicitly telling the supplier it must be able to handle highly corrosive chemicals. The supplier assures the buyer the pump will work for this specific use. The pump later fails due to corrosion. Which warranty has primarily been breached?
options: Implied warranty of fitness for a particular purpose
questions.explain: The implied warranty of fitness for a particular purpose applies when a buyer relies on the seller's skill or judgment to select suitable goods, and the seller knows the specific purpose for which the goods are required.
questions.subject: CPPB Domain I: Regulatory & Compliance

questions.q: A buyer purchases standard printer paper from a vendor without any specific discussions about the quality. It is assumed the paper will be of average, acceptable quality and pass without objection in the trade. This assumption is protected by:
options: The Implied Warranty of Fitness for a Particular Purpose
questions.explain: The implied warranty of merchantability requires that goods sold by a merchant be fit for the ordinary purposes for which they are used and conform to standard trade quality.
questions.subject: CPPB Domain I: Regulatory & Compliance

questions.q: A warranty of title under the UCC guarantees the buyer that:
options: The goods are of acceptable quality in the trade.
The goods will last for at least one year.
The seller owns the goods, has the right to transfer them, and they are free from any unknown liens or encumbrances.
The title documentation has been notarized by an attorney.
questions.explain: The UCC Warranty of Title promises that the seller is the rightful owner of the goods, the transfer is rightful, and the goods are free from security interests or liens unknown to the buyer.
